description:
FILED s522a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-19) from the #3061 acceptance runs: Text-CSV-2.04's t/util.pl transpiles now, and 15 t/ files run rows they never ran.  Every row below was checked against TWO emulations under real perl 5.40.3 (scratch/s522a/fu/run.sh: utf8::is_utf8 forced to 1 = #1389; fu/run2.sh: that PLUS Text::CSV_PP's `%{$self->{_CACHE}} = %$ctx` stores removed = #3611) and is NOT reproduced by either -- so it is a different mechanism.  Outputs: scratch/s522a/csv/<file>.out in the s522a worktree.

LOUD (pre-existing mechanism, newly reached).  t/90_csv.t lines 292-296: `my $x = sub { 42 }; eval { csv (in => $tfn, out => \$x) }` -- perl: "Not a GLOB reference", PCL: "Can't use string (\"_90test.csv\") as an ARRAY ref while \"strict refs\" in use" -- so a DIFFERENT path is taken (not just message text: the error names the INPUT file name), and the file later stops at row 117 of 128 with rc 2.  NEXT STEP: minimise Text::CSV_PP::csv's `out` dispatch on a reference to a CODE-holding scalar (ref(\$x) is REF in perl).


=== DONE (s538a, Opus, 2026-11-12; commits 39c945d9 + 8a5775c4, cl/ only) ===
perl's rv2gv kills `open($fh, ...)` when $fh holds \$code, [1], {}, a code ref or \5 -- before the open, so no file is
created.  PCL overwrote the variable with the new handle and the open succeeded: Text::CSV_PP's `csv(in => $f, out =>
\$code)` then opened its INPUT through the out-handle.  %p-fh-place-check (every opener's install slot) asks
%p-stat-handle-shaped-p, the one handle-designator predicate.  The file's NEXT stop: `$out ||= \*STDOUT` / `our $g =
\*STDOUT` (p-or-assign -> p-setf -> p-scalar-=) held the glob-ref wrapper box-in-box, so `$g->print` died "unblessed
reference"; the reference branch now box-sets a glob wrapper.  Guards Pl/t/open-modes-01.t rows 11 + 12,
inverse-verified.  The USE slots (print / close / readline / eof / binmode / fileno) are #4842.
BOARD: Text-CSV 90_csv.t (perl 128): base 116 ok / 1 not ok, rc 255 -> 128 / 0 PASS.  CLOSE-WITH-ROWS: 90_csv.t row 104 + *PLAN*
(#3618) left the board baseline.
